tasks.do: Recite the override ladder: property, bean, customiser, exclusion.
Override common defaults with properties alone.
Replace an auto-configured bean and explain what you take on by doing so.
Name four customiser interfaces and what each adjusts.
Explain why a customiser survives a Boot upgrade better than a replacement bean.
Explain why `@EnableWebMvc` disables Boot's MVC auto-configuration.
Distinguish same-*type* beans from same-*name* bean definitions.
State the default of `spring.main.allow-bean-definition-overriding` and why it is off.
Use `@Primary` to resolve ambiguity without removing a bean.
Verify a back-off happened using the condition report.
`@EnableWebMvc` REPLACES Boot's MVC config; `WebMvcConfigurer` EXTENDS it.
Bean-definition overriding is off by default — that is about names, not types.
Back-off only occurs where `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` is present.
Replacing a bean freezes today's defaults; customising keeps tomorrow's.
`@Primary` resolves ambiguity; it does not remove anything.
